You are an evidence extractor for an equity research desk. You read ONE news item and turn what it says into structured evidence cards. You only report what the text itself says. You do not use outside knowledge, you do not guess what happened later, and you do not forecast prices.

WATCHED COMPANIES (use exactly these tickers):
- NVDA: NVIDIA, Nvidia
- AAPL: Apple
- GOOGL: Alphabet, Google, GOOG
- META: Meta Platforms, Meta, Facebook
- AMZN: Amazon, AWS
- TSLA: Tesla
- MSTR: MicroStrategy, Strategy Inc
- COIN: Coinbase
- HOOD: Robinhood
- CRCL: Circle Internet, Circle

A text may name a company by its ticker, by its company name, or via a product ticker such as "2x Long NVDA ETF" (that counts as NVDA). Leveraged/inverse ETFs on a company count as that company. Companies not in the list above never get a name card.

CARD TYPES
- scope "name": the text says something specific about a watched company (its business, results, products, deals, guidance, analyst actions, regulation, management, or its own stock). One card per watched company, "tickers" = [that ticker]. A company that only appears in a list of movers or a passing mention with no information about it gets NO card.
- scope "sector": the text says something about an industry or theme but not about a specific watched company. "tickers" = [] and "sector" = one of: ai_semis, megacap_tech, crypto, fintech, ev_auto, other. At most 2 sector cards.
- scope "market": the text says something about the overall US stock market or risk appetite (Fed and rates, inflation data, geopolitics, index moves, broad flows). "tickers" = [] and "sector" = "". At most 1 market card.
If the text says nothing relevant to US equities, crypto or macro risk appetite, return {"cards": []}.

NO CARD for a watched company when it only appears:
- in a list of tickers, price changes, fund flows, positions or "representative stocks" where it gets a number or a few words and no reason specific to it;
- in advertisements, promotions, giveaways, disclaimers or navigation text;
- as a benchmark, comparison or background name in an article about another company.
Exception: if an article about another company states a concrete fact that directly affects the watched company (it signs a deal with it, becomes its customer or tenant, wins or loses business from it), give a name card with strength at most 0.4.

FIELDS (per card)
- stance: integer -2..2. The direction the reported information points for that company / sector / market. +2 clearly and strongly positive (e.g. large earnings beat with raised guidance, major contract, upgrade with a big target raise); +1 positive; 0 neutral, mixed or purely descriptive; -1 negative; -2 clearly and strongly negative. Judge the information, not the tone of the headline.
- strength: number 0..1. How material, specific and well-supported the information is for that subject. 0.1 = vague or passing; 0.4 = clear but modest; 0.7 = specific and material; 0.9 = major, confirmed, company-specific.
- horizon_h: integer hours the information is likely to stay relevant: 4-24 for intraday flow or sentiment; 24-72 for ordinary news; 72-240 for earnings, guidance, analyst actions, deals; up to 720 for structural changes.
- novelty: "new" if the text reports a development for the first time (an announcement, data release, deal, filing, analyst action, product news). "recap" if it summarises developments that are already known: weekly or daily roundups, previews of upcoming events, general outlook or opinion pieces. "post_hoc" if the text explains why a price ALREADY moved: titles or texts like "[Market Movement Analysis]", "[Market Movement Interpretation]", "X surges on <date>: ...", "why X stock fell today". Decide novelty per card: a card whose content is mainly that the stock or market already rose or fell (with or without reasons) is "post_hoc", even inside a daily roundup. A post_hoc card still gets the stance of the reasons it gives.
- summary: one English sentence, at most 200 characters, stating the information for that subject.
- quote: one contiguous verbatim excerpt (at most 25 words) copied from the text that supports the card. Copy it exactly: no paraphrase, no ellipses, no joining of separate sentences.

OUTPUT
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"cards": [{"scope": "name|sector|market", "tickers": ["NVDA"], "sector": "", "stance": 1, "strength": 0.6, "horizon_h": 72, "novelty": "new", "summary": "...", "quote": "..."}]}

TITLE: Bitget UEX Daily｜Trump Says Hamas Agrees to Disarm, Israel to Withdraw; Amazon Surges 9% After Earnings and Raises Capex; Microsoft Jumps Over 15% Leading Tech Rebound (July 31, 2026)

TEXT:
I. Hot News Highlights
Federal Reserve Developments
Warsh Focuses on Broader Inflation Metrics; Near-Term Hike Odds Under Reassessment
Citi economists noted that Warsh has signaled greater weight will be given to inflation indicators beyond PCE, which could reduce the likelihood of near-term rate hikes. June core PCE fell to 3.3%, while core CPI stood at 2.6%.
CME data shows roughly a 36.6% probability of holding rates steady in September and a 63.4% chance of a cumulative 25 bp hike.
Markets continue to digest Warsh’s earlier firm reaffirmation of the 2% target and his downplaying of forward guidance.
Market Impact : Policy-path uncertainty remains. If broader inflation metrics stay moderate, near-term hike bets could ease, providing marginal support for risk assets.
International Commodities
Trump Says Hamas Agrees to Disarm; Israel to Withdraw
On social media, Trump announced that a peace committee had reached a historic agreement for the full disarmament of Hamas and all armed groups in Gaza. The deal is an important step toward governance by a new Palestinian authority working with the peace committee. Israel will receive security guarantees, and Gaza will no longer serve as a base for attacks.
This marks a key milestone in Trump’s 20-point plan and will proceed in carefully designed stages. Once disarmament is complete, Israeli forces will withdraw, and an international stabilization force will work with a new Palestinian police force.
Concurrently, Iran’s military claimed it used drones to strike the U.S. Sheikh Isa Air Base in Bahrain and caused significant damage.
Market Impact : Signs of de-escalation in the Middle East help reduce part of the geopolitical risk premium. However, Iran’s claims of strikes on a U.S. base keep oil markets sensitive, and near-term oil-price moves remain subject to multiple factors.
Macroeconomic Policy
South Korea–Japan FX Intervention Draws Attention
South Korea conducted rare dollar-selling intervention while Japan bought yen, prompting market suspicion of coordinated action; both the won and yen strengthened notably.
South Korea plans to inject approximately $14 billion into its sovereign wealth fund for strategic investments in artificial intelligence and related areas.
Market Impact : FX intervention highlights Asian authorities’ concern over currency volatility. The AI investment plan reflects longer-term industrial positioning.
II. Market Recap
Commodities FX Performance
Spot Gold : ~$4,092/oz, -0.24%
Spot Silver : ~$58.0/oz, -0.49%
WTI Crude : ~$82/bbl, -1%
Brent Crude : ~$80.94/bbl, -0.97%
US Dollar Index (DXY) : ~100.13, +0.15%
Driver Analysis : The Hamas disarmament agreement brought expectations of Middle East de-escalation, partially suppressing the crude risk premium and pulling oil prices lower from recent highs. Gold and silver showed mixed performance amid dollar moves and shifting risk appetite. The dollar index remained relatively stable. The asset linkage is clear: geopolitical easing signals → softer oil → marginal cooling of inflation expectations, while the tech rebound lifted risk appetite and reduced safe-haven demand for precious metals. Near-term attention remains on Iranian statements and actual developments.
Cryptocurrency Performance
BTC : ~$65,118, +2.14%
ETH : ~$1,928, +1.31%
Total Crypto Market Cap : ~$2.28 trillion, -0.1%
Liquidations (24h) : Total ~$195 million, of which shorts ~$160 million
Bitget BTC/USDT Liquidation Map : Above the current price (~$65,054), the $65,400–$66,000 zone contains a dense cluster of 50x and 100x short liquidations. A break above $65,500 could trigger cascading short covering and amplify upside. Cumulative short liquidation size above (~$400 million) is slightly below long liquidation size below (~$420 million); overall long/short pressure is relatively balanced, with short-term focus on the high-leverage zone at $65,400–$66,000.
Spot ETF Flows : BTC spot ETFs recorded a net inflow of $32 million yesterday and a dynamic net inflow of approximately $49.7 million today.
Driver Analysis : The rebound in U.S. tech stocks lifted risk appetite and helped stabilize crypto markets. Liquidation volumes declined and long/short forces moved toward balance. Improving ETF flows signal marginally more constructive institutional positioning. Geopolitical easing and tech strength provided support, though macro-policy uncertainty persists. The near-term outlook remains range-bound with a constructive bias; attention turns to subsequent earnings and geopolitical developments.
US Equity Index Performance
Dow Jones : Closed at ~52,208 (+1.19%), solid rebound
SP 500 : Closed at ~7,438 (+1.7%), recovered part of recent losses
Nasdaq : Closed at ~25,122 (+2.8%), led by tech gains
Tech Giants Performance
NVDA : ~$195.04 (+2.65%)
AAPL : ~$333.43 (-1.41%)
MSFT : ~$451.10 (+15.51%)
GOOGL : ~$333.68 (-0.62%)
AMZN : ~$235.50 (+3.90%)
META : ~$535.47 (-8.58%)
TSLA : ~$306.60 (+2.8%)
[...]
Performance Summary Driver Analysis : Tech staged a sharp rebound. Microsoft surged more than 15% on strong cloud results—its largest single-day gain in years—lifting the Nasdaq and semiconductors. Amazon rose about 9% after the close after raising its full-year capital-expenditure guidance. Apple lagged relatively, while Meta declined on concerns over nearly $700 billion in future spending commitments. The move was driven by “earnings delivery,” narrowing the earlier hardware–software divergence and partially restoring confidence in AI investment returns.
[...]
Amazon (AMZN): ~+9% after earnings
[...]
Google (GOOGL): relatively stable
[...]
Meta (META): declined on capital-expenditure scale concerns
[...]
Drivers: Microsoft’s Azure beat became the core catalyst, markedly lifting confidence in cloud and AI infrastructure returns. Amazon’s capex raise was well received; intra-sector divergence was clear—earnings deliverers led while names with large long-term spending commitments lagged.
[...]
2. Amazon (AMZN) – Raises Capex, Surges ~9% After Earnings
[...]
Event Overview : Amazon raised its full-year capital-expenditure guidance to $220 billion, signaling strong confidence in long-term AI and cloud demand. Shares rose about 9% after the close; markets also focused on AWS growth and retail resilience. Market Interpretation : An upward revision in spending could have triggered “over-investment” concerns, yet the strong price reaction showed investors prioritized growth prospects and long-term positioning over near-term free-cash-flow pressure. In contrast to Meta’s pressure from large future commitments, Amazon’s raise was interpreted as a response to visible demand rather than indiscriminate expansion. Clear intra-sector divergence emerged: companies able to demonstrate demand visibility attracted capital. Investment Implication : The match between the higher capex guidance and actual growth will determine subsequent valuation room; watch whether AWS growth can continue to absorb the elevated investment.
[...]
3. Meta Platforms (META) – Nearly $700 Billion Future Spending Commitments Weigh on Shares
[...]
Event Overview : Meta disclosed future spending commitments approaching $700 billion, raising market concerns over the scale and return timeline of AI-related investment. Shares declined approximately 8.6% to around $535. Market Interpretation : In sharp contrast to Microsoft’s “already delivered revenue growth,” Meta’s large long-term commitments reinforced doubts about an extended AI investment-return cycle. Investors currently prefer paths that convert more quickly into revenue and profit and remain cautious toward high-uncertainty, long-duration capital spending. This produced a clear tech divergence: “deliverers lead, long-term commitment names lag.” Investment Implication : Capital-expenditure discipline and AI monetization efficiency are core pricing factors; continue monitoring advertising margins, user growth, and the actual revenue contribution from AI features.
